rounds.response:
EU checkout p95 improved but 5xxs remain ~2x baseline with an estimated SLA breach risk in ~60 minutes and request Finance approve a standard short-term EU log-ingest burst from our approved observability vendor to restore full request-level traces.  
Lower-cost mitigations attempted and ruled out: increased sampling and endpoint-focused trace collection (dropped distributed spans linking 5xxs to downstream calls), local temporary log retention (insufficient cross-service correlation), targeted log-level elevation (too noisy and slow to analyze), and rerouting non-critical logs (would omit the error traces we need), so none reliably recover the missing traces for fast RCA.  
I recommend a 24–48 hour burst sized at ~3x current EU ingestion (midpoint of the 2–4x range previously proposed) using the vendor’s documented short-term burst add-on.  
Next 15–30 minutes: continue incremental EU checkout scaling, pause/rollback suspect deploys, tighten circuit-breakers and backoff, escalate DB/queue replica scaling where latency shows contention, and monitor error-rate and p95 every 5 minutes while the ETL owner throttles nonessential ETL work and watches queue length.  
Please approve Finance to provision the burst now; SRE will monitor usage, terminate the burst once 5xxs return to baseline and traces confirm RCA, and I’ll provide a 30-minute update.
